original_question: Find formal normal forms and formal invariants for germs tangent to the identity whose characteristic directions are all degenerate.
target_in_paper: Section 3.5, OP16: the open problem asking to find formal normal forms and invariants for germs tangent to the identity having (possibly only) degenerate characteristic directions.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the formal-classification aspect of the problem, the class of holomorphic germs tangent to the identity, and the fact that the unresolved case is tied to degenerate characteristic directions.
missing_details: The relevant equivalence relation is formal conjugacy, not holomorphic or topological conjugacy: one seeks normal forms and invariants under f1 = Φ^{-1} ◦ f2 ◦ Φ for an invertible formal map Φ in C0[[z1,...,zn]]^n.
The ambient category is holomorphic local dynamical systems f in End(C^n,O), equivalently convergent n-tuples in C0{z1,...,zn}^n over the field C.
A tangent-to-the-identity germ must be written as f(z) = z + P_ν(z) + P_{ν+1}(z) + ..., where P_ν is the first nonzero homogeneous term and ν >= 2 is the multiplicity.
A characteristic direction is a nonzero vector v in C^n such that P_ν(v) = λv for some λ in C; it is degenerate exactly when λ = 0, equivalently P_ν(v) = 0.

The paper's formulation is not limited to the case where all characteristic directions are degenerate; it asks about germs having degenerate characteristic directions, possibly as their only characteristic directions.
No dimension restriction is imposed in OP16; the question is stated for arbitrary n.
OP16 does not assume that the origin is an isolated fixed point; importing that hypothesis would confuse it with the different problem OP13.

The surrounding motivation is that Theorem 16 gives a formal classification in a nondegenerate-characteristic-direction regime, and OP16 asks how to extend or complete that classification when degenerate characteristic directions are present.

No nilpotency condition and no asymptotic clause of the form 'for all sufficiently large m' appears in this problem; a faithful stand-alone version should make clear that no such extra hypotheses are part of the statement.
refined_question: How can one complete the formal classification, up to formal conjugacy, of holomorphic germs f in End(C^n,O) tangent to the identity and of multiplicity ν >= 2, written as f(z) = z + P_ν(z) + P_{ν+1}(z) + ..., by finding formal normal forms and formal invariants for those germs having degenerate characteristic directions (possibly as their only characteristic directions), where a characteristic direction is a nonzero v in C^n with P_ν(v) = λv and is degenerate when P_ν(v) = 0?
justification: The draft is targeting OP16 in Section 3.5. The paper first sets up the formal-classification problem in Section 1 via Q5 and Definition 4, where 'normal forms and invariants' are explicitly with respect to formal conjugacy in C0[[z1,...,zn]]^n. In Section 3.4 it defines tangent-to-the-identity germs as f(z) = z + P_ν + ... with ν >= 2 and defines characteristic and degenerate characteristic directions. Then, immediately before OP16, Theorem 16 states an Écalle formal classification result for a regime with only nondegenerate characteristic directions; the paper then asks how to complete the formal classification in the presence of degenerate characteristic directions. Your draft is close to the official problem, but it is slightly too narrow because OP16 includes mixed cases as well, not only germs whose characteristic directions are all degenerate.
